speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned sudden-onset vertigo; to begin my assessment, have you experienced any hearing loss, tinnitus, or a feeling of fullness in your affected ear?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). Given the sudden onset lasting only 3 minutes with resolution to baseline and no hearing symptoms, this is highly characteristic of BPPV. I will now proceed with the Dix-Hallpike maneuver to confirm the diagnosis.
